items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9463

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to compensation,
benefits and other terms and conditions of employment of state officers
and employees who are the members of the security supervisors unit; to
amend the state finance law, in relation to the employee benefit fund
for all members of the security supervisors unit; to amend the civil
service law, in relation to increases in salary payable to certain offi-
cers and employees; to authorize funding of joint labor-management
committees; to implement an agreement between the state and the employee
organization representing the members of the security supervisors unit;
to repeal certain provisions of the civil service law relating thereto;
and making an appropriation for the purpose of effectuating certain
provisions thereof

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would implement the terms of a collectively negotiated agree-
ment between the State of New York ("State") and Council 82, the employ-
ee organization representing members of the collective negotiating unit
designated as the Security Supervisors Unit (the "Unit"), entered into
pursuant to Civil Service Law ("CSL") Article 14 (the "Agreement").

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill would repeal CSL § 130(1)(i) and add a new CSL §
130(1)(i), to provide for the application of salary schedules to those
members of the Unit who are employed by the Department of Corrections
and Community Supervision ("DOCCS") and are designated as peace officers
pursuant to Criminal Procedure Law ("CPL") § 2.10(25) who are eligible
for arbitration ("the arbitration-eligible members").

Section 2 of the bill would repeal CSL § 130(1)(b) and add a new CSL §
130(1)(b) to provide for the application of salary schedules to those
members of the Unit who are not eligible for binding interest arbi-
tration pursuant to CSL § 209(4) (the "arbitration-ineligible members").

Section 3 of the bill would amend State Finance Law ("SFL") § 207-a
(2-a) to continue employer payments to the employee benefit fund estab-
lished by Council 82, for the benefit of all members of the Unit in the
amounts agreed to by the parties in each year of the Agreement.

Section 4 of the bill would amend subparagraphs 1 and 2 of paragraph (e)
of CSL Section 130(1), as added by Part B of Chapter 60 of the Laws of
2022 (the pay bill for members of the Rent Regulation Services Unit
represented by District Council 37) to make a technical corrections to
the salary schedules.

Section 5 of the bill would provide for increases in the compensation
applicable to certain arbitration-ineligible. members of the Unit, in
accordance with the terms of the Agreement, as follows:

Paragraph (1) would provide that the section applies to all full-time
members of the Unit who are arbitration-ineligible.


Paragraphs (2), (3), (4), (5), (6) and (9) would provide all full-time
annual salaried members of the Unit who are arbitration-ineligible with
a 2% increase in compensation over and above the annual salary they
received as of March 31, effective April 1, in the years 2016, 2017,
2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022, respectively.

Paragraph (7) would move all full-time annual salaried members of the
Unit who are arbitration-ineligible to the salary schedule applicable to
arbitration-eligible members of the Unit, effective April 1, 2021, and
increase their compensation accordingly.

Paragraph (8) would increase the 25-year longevity applicable to full-
time annual salary members of the Unit who are arbitration-ineligible by
$500, effective October 1, 2021.

Paragraph (10) would provide performance advance payments to all annual
salaried members of the Unit who are arbitration-ineligible within their
salary grades pursuant to CSL § 131 (6).

Paragraph (11) would continue to provide that annual salaried, arbitra-
tion-ineligible members who are eligible forthe 10,15, 20 and 25-year
longevity step payments would receive such payments as prescribed by CSL
§ 130(1)(b).

Paragraph (12) would provide that where the salary of any annual sala-
ried, arbitration-ineligible member of the Unit covered by this section
is identical with either the hiring rate; performance advance steps
1,2,3,4 or 5; the job rate; or the 10, 15, 20 or 25-year longevity step
such member's basic annual salary would be increased to the correspond-
ing hiring rate, performance advance step, job rate or longevity step as
prescribed by CSL § 130(1)(b).

Paragraph (13) would afford unencumbered or newly created positions
within the Unit the same treatment as encumbered and currently existing
positions under this section, and would provide that the Director of the
Budget may reduce the salary of any position in the Unit which is or
becomes vacant.

Paragraph (14) would provide that the increases payable pursuant to this
section, except those in paragraphs ten, eleven and twelve, shall apply
on a prorated basis to eligible members of the Unit who are paid on an
hourly or per diem basis and members serving on a part-time or seasonal
basis.

Paragraph (15) would provide that the increases payable pursuant to this
section shall not apply to arbitration-ineligible members of the Unit
who are paid on a fee schedule basis.

Paragraph (16) would give the Director of the Budget the discretion to
apply the appropriate increases provided for in this section to eligible
members of the Unit who are in annual-salaried positions that are not
allocated to salary grades.

Paragraph (17) would give the Director of the Budget and the Director of
Employee Relations the discretion to withhold all of, or a portion of, a
Unit member's increase in compensation when such increase is not
warranted or is not appropriate.

Section 6 of the bill would provide for increases in the compensation
applicable to certain arbitration-eligible members of the Unit, in
accordance with the terms of the Agreement, as follows:

Paragraph (1) would provide that the section applies to all full-time
members of the Unit who are arbitration-eligible.

Paragraphs (2), (3), (4), (5), (6), (7) and (9) would provide all full-
time annual salaried members of the Unit who are arbitration-eligible
with a 2% increase in compensation over and above the annual salary they
received as of March 31, effective April 1, in the years 2016, 2017,
2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022, respectively.

Paragraph (8) would increase the 25-year longevity applicable to full-
time annual salary members of the Unit who are arbitration-eligible by
$500, effective October 1, 2021.

Paragraph (10) would provide performance advance payments to all annual
salaried members of the Unit who are arbitration-eligible within their
salary grades pursuant to CSL § 131(6).

Paragraph (11) would continue to provide that annual salaried, arbitra-
tion-eligible members who are eligible for the 10,15, 20 and 25-year
longevity step payments would receive such payments as prescribed by CSL
§ 130(1)(i).

Paragraph (12) would provide that where the salary of any annual sala-
ried, arbitration-eligible member of the Unit covered by this section is
identical with either the hiring rate; performance advance steps 1,2,3,4
or 5; the job rate; or the 10, 15, 20 or 25-year longevity step such
member's basic annual salary would be increased to the corresponding
hiring rate, performance advance step, job rate or longevity step as
prescribed by CS! §§ 130(1)(i).

Paragraph (13) would afford unencumbered or newly created positions
within the Unit the same treatment as encumbered and currently existing
positions under this section and would provide that the Director of the
Budget may reduce the salary of any position in the Unit which is or
becomes vacant.

Paragraph (14) would provide that the increases payable pursuant to this
section, except those in paragraphs ten, eleven and twelve, shall apply
on a prorated basis to eligible members of the Unit who are paid on an
hourly or per diem basis and members serving on a part-time or seasonal
basis.

Paragraph (15) would provide that the increases payable pursuant to this
section shall not apply to arbitration-eligible members of the Unit who
are paid on a fee schedule basis.

Paragraph (16) would give the Director of the Budget the discretion to
apply the appropriate increases provided for in this section to eligible
members of the Unit who are in annual-salaried positions that are not
allocated to salary grades.

Paragraph (17) would give the Director of the Budget and the Director of
Employee Relations the discretion to withhold all of, or a portion of, a

Unit member's increase in compensation when such increase is not
warranted or is not appropriate.

Section 7 of the bill would continue the additional compensation paid to
all full-time annual salaried members of the Unit for assembling for
briefing prior to the commencement of duties ("pre-shift briefing") in
accordance with the terms of the Agreement and CSI. § 134(5); would
provide that members of the Unit who are in non-pay status for the day
would not receive such pre-shift briefing compensation; and would
provide that pre-shift briefing compensation would be excluded from a
Unit member's annual salary as overtime pay but included for retirement
purposes:

Section 8 of the bill would provide for increases in command pay.
Effective April 1, 2019, security supervisors command pay shall be
increased by $1,100 to $2,874. Then, solely for the period from April 1,
2019 through March 31, 2022, security supervisors command pay shall be
increased by $500 annually to $3,374. Effective April 1, 2022, security
supervisors command pay shall be $2,874 per year.  These payments shall
be equally divided over the 26 payroll periods in each fiscal year and
shall count as compensation for overtime and retirement purposes.

Section 9 of the bill would authorize hazardous duty pay for full-time
annual salaried members of the Unit, consistent with the terms of the
Agreement, after one year of service. For arbitration-ineligible
members, effective April 1, 2019, the annual payment shall be $150,
which shall be increased to $200 effective April 1, 2020. For arbitra-
tion-eligible members, the annual payment shall be as follows:  $750
effective April 1, 2019; $950 effective April 1, 2020; $1,150 effective
April 1, 2021; and $1,500 effective October 1, 2021. These payments
shall be equally divided over the 26 payroll periods in each fiscal year
and shall count as compensation for overtime and retirement purposes.

Section 10 of the bill would continue and increase the location pay
benefit for full-time annual salaried arbitration-ineligible members of
the Unit, as follows:

Full-time salaried arbitration-ineligible members of the Unit whose
official work station is in the County of Monroe who on March 31, 1985

Section 11 of the bill would continue and increase the location pay
benefit for full-time annual salaried arbitration-eligible members of
the Unit, as follows:

Section 12 of the bill would continue the payment of location compen-
sation for certain employees of the Hudson Valley Developmental Disabil-
ities Services Office who currently receive location pay in accordance
with specified provisions of law.

Section 13 of the bill would continue the inconvenience pay program for
full-time annual salaried arbitration ineligible members of the Unit who
work four or more hours between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.,
except on an overtime basis, at the rate of $626 per year

Section 14 of the bill would continue the inconvenience pay program for
arbitration-eligible members of the Unit employed by DOCCS at the rate
of $1,928 per year for the evening shift and at the rate of $964 per
year for the night shift.

Section 15 of the bill would require the State, in accordance with the
terms of the Agreement, to contribute designated amounts to the accounts
of eligible employees who are enrolled for dependent care deductions
pursuant to State Finance Law ("SR") § 201-a(7).

Section 16 of the bill would continue the state-wide joint labor-manage-
ment committee for the period April 1, 2016 through March 31, 2023, with
funding in the amounts provided in the Agreement

Section 17 of the bill would make the appropriations contained in this
bill available to the State for the payment and publication of grievance
and arbitration settlements and awards.

Section 18 of the bill would continue to exempt the salaries of newly
hired members of the Unit from the imposition of the "salary deferral"
program pursuant to SFL § 200(2-a).

Section 19 of the bill establishes the methodology for establishing the
date upon which eligible members of the Unit would be eligible to
receive the salary increases and deferred payment of salary increases
provided for by the Agreement.

Section 20 of the bill would provide a lump-sum payment to each incum-
bent member of the Unit to cover the difference between the salary and
compensation such member would receive subsequent to the enactment of
this bill as compared with the salary and compensation that such members
received prior to its enactment. This section also would provide that,
pursuant to the agreement, effective the pay period for which overtime
earned as of April 1, 2019 would be paid, the overtime earned subsequent
to April 1, 2019 shall be recalculated, to reflect a denominator used
for purposes of calculating overtime, and such recalculation will be
reconciled, adjusted and applied against the retroactive payment refer-
enced herein. In addition, this section would provide that no lump sum

payment shall be made to any member of the Unit who was terminated from
employment pursuant to a disciplinary termination.

Section 21 of the bill would authorize the State Comptroller to pay any
amounts required by the provisions of this bill.

Section 22 of the bill provides that the salary increases and lump sum
payments provided for in this bill shall not be implemented until the
Director of Employee Relations has delivered a letter to the Director of
the Budget and the Comptroller certifying that there is in effect with
respect to such negotiating unit a collectively negotiated agreement,
ratified by the membership, which provides for such increases and
modifications, and which are fully executed in writing with the state
pursuant to article 14 of the civil service.

Sections 23 and 24 of the bill would appropriate monies to pay for the
personal service, nonpe sonal services, and labor management committee
costs provided for in this bill.

Section 25 of the bill would make this bill effective immediately and
deem it to have been in full force and effect on and after April 1,
2016.

 
EXISTING LAW:

* L. 2012, c. 257 sets forth terms and conditions of employment for
arbitration-ineligible and arbitration eligible members of the Unit
arising out of the collective bargaining agreement between the State of
New York and Council 82 for the period of April 1, 2009 through March
31, 2016.

* CSL § 130(1)(b) establishes the current salary and longevity schedules
for arbitration-ineligible members of the Unit.

* CSL § 130(1)(i) establishes the current salary and longevity schedules
for arbitration-eligible members of the Unit.

* CSL § 134(5) establishes additional compensation for employees in any
positions ineligible for overtime who are required to work beyond a
normal work week.

* SFL § 207-a (2-a) establishes the current employee benefit fund for
members of the unit.

* L2022, c. 60, Part B sets forth the terms and conditions of employment
arising out of the collective bargaining agreement between the State and
District Council 37 covering members of the Rent Regulation Services
Unit, including the salary schedules as codified in subparagraphs 1 and
2 of Section 130(1)(e) of the Civil Service Law.

 
STATEMENT IN SUPPORT:

This bill is necessary to implement the terms of a collective bargaining
agreement between the State. and Council 82, the employee organization
representing members of the Unit, entered into pursuant to CSL Article
14.

 
BUDGET IMPLICATIONS:
This bill would provide appropriations totaling approximately $53
million to pay for the cost of the Agreement during the period of April
1,2016 to March 31, 2023.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill would take effect immediately and be deemed to have been in
full force and effect on and after April 1, 2016.
